newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X shares slide in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X shares slide in heavy trading.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd fell further on Friday, extending their week-long slide on rumors and investor jitters.
Bre-X dropped 0.50 to 21.40 on almost one million shares at midday on the Toronto Stock Exchange. The stock has fallen from 23.65 at the beginning of the week.

"It's been trading in the range between 19 and 25 since the summer," said analyst Dorothy Atkinson with Whalen Beliveau in Vancouver. "I really think it will continue to trade within this range depending on the rumor of the day, depending on the rumor of the hour."
Rumors have been rampant this week, with some investors tiring of the uncertainty, analysts said. Bre-X officials would not return calls to confirm or deny the rumors.

Bre-X stock has been volatile since doubts about the ownership of its massive Busang gold discovery in Indonesia became public this autumn. The Indonesian government has delayed issuing Bre-X essential contracts of work until the dispute is settled.
The ownership dispute has clouded Bre-X's search for a major gold producer to act as operator and possible owner of Busang.
The world's biggest gold producers are said to have an eye on the discovery, including Barrick Gold Corp, North America's biggest gold company.
Barrick chairman Peter Munk was in Jakarta on Friday, but Barrick officials could not be reached for elaboration.
